messages:
ashwin: FYI — saw a p99 blip for short requests after the kernel switchover yesterday. profiler + trace look like short sequences get queued behind long seq microbatches; KV miss rate for short lanes spikes. attaching quick dump.

ashwin: flamegraph snippet (trimmed):
```
0x0 kernel_fastpath  35%
0x1 kernel_sched    22%
0x2 kv_lookup       18% (misses 2x for short seqs)
0x3 batch_admit     15%
0x4 other           10%
```

morgan: can you confirm this is after the kernel-selection change (the one that favors full-simd kernels for long runs)?

ashwin: yes — change was deployed at 1768960000. The interesting bit: token_budget_target still set to 16 tokens/mini-batch which seems to let long sequences form larger contiguous microbatches that delay short lane admission.

taylor: hypothesis: admission knob + a short-path reserve should help. proposal: short_path_reserve=0.2, token_credit_smoothing=ema_alpha=0.6, per-tenant cap for long lanes. quick config sketch: 
```yaml
batcher:
  short_path_reserve: 0.2  # fraction of mini-batches kept for short lanes
  token_credit:
    target: 16
    smoothing: 0.6
kv:
  prefetch_for_short: true
  prefetch_threshold_tokens: 32
```

sara: we rolled a similar prefetch + reserve in canary-3426. p99 for short seqs improved ~12%, but we saw ~3% throughput drop for long-heavy workloads. tradeoff depends on SLA.

lee: alternative: allow short lanes to preempt a single microbatch every N ms if their p50 > SLA. i.e. time-based handoff instead of static reserve. cheaper than stealing capacity continuously.

deploy-bot: canary launched: infra/canary/continuous-batcher/2026-03-18-02 (id: canary-4871)

ashwin: I'll run a focused canary with three knobs: 1) short_path_reserve=0.2 2) token_credit_smoothing=0.7 (exp smoothing) 3) kv_prefetch for tokens <=32. PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/457 — test infra + telemetry hooks included.

morgan: add these telemetry metrics before the canary: 
- per_tenant.short_vs_long_p99_ratio
- kv_miss_rate_by_seq_len_bucket (0-32,33-128,>128)
- admitted_batch_size_distribution

taylor: also add a kernel-hint metric: prefer fastpath kernel when avg_seq_len<64 && kv_hit_rate>0.6. This should reduce kernel-swap overhead when short lanes dominate.

sara: +1 — and capture per-kernel context-switch counts (we suspect switches cause queuing jitter).

ashwin: noted. running canary now against two synthetic mixes: (A) 80/20 short/long, (B) 20/80 short/long. will report back with flamegraphs + p50/p95/p99 and total token/sec in ~6h.

lee: if the canary looks good, let's try a staged rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback on short.p99 > baseline * 1.15.

morgan: thanks — if ashwin needs help with the telemetry dashboards ping me and i'll add widgets for quick comparison. :thumbsup:

ashwin: thanks all, will update thread with results.
